metadata.description: Claude Code plugins by Lee Driscoll: an interoperating stack of hub, cadence, domains, work and intent.

plugins.name: hub
plugins.description: The stack's front door: reports what is installed and what each component's version is, runs the guided upgrade across every owner in order, and collates every other plugin's doctor into one report. Resolves a role to the plugin that serves it via a published roster contract, so an in-house plugin is bootstrapped the same way an official one is. Declares no dependencies and is required by nothing.

plugins.name: cadence
plugins.description: A configurable project-management methodology: vision -> roadmap -> epics -> tickets -> gates, worked in bounded sessions. Binds to your tracker/VCS/docs via adapters, and to your team's process via a flow spec (solo, team-sprints, live-oncall, or your own authored flow). Includes /cadence:doctor to check a project's setup.

plugins.name: domains
plugins.description: Project memory: per-topic operational-knowledge files a repo authors about itself, with a manifest that maps a task's topics to the files worth loading. `domains init` scaffolds the knowledge system; `domains migrate` upgrades it. Publishes a doc-system contract so any tool can find what applies without reading this plugin's files.

plugins.name: work
plugins.description: Portable domain-system + ticket-workflow skill. `work init` bootstraps per-project operational-knowledge files and the `prep` commands; `work on <TICKET>` delivers a tracked ticket end-to-end via subagent orchestration. Detects the environment, VCS, and ticket tracker rather than assuming them.

plugins.name: intent
plugins.description: Capture a project's design as an authoritative intent layer: what the maintainer says the system is FOR, dictated rather than read off the code, with every contradiction between stated intent and implementation logged as a tracked gap. Publishes an intent-read contract so a tool can ask what applies to what it is about to touch — and exposes no write operation at any tier, because the code gets no vote.
